sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro preview — Gemini API model documentation
sources.evidence: Lists customtools as a Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview version, supplies shared capabilities and a model-card link, and identifies its custom-tool prioritization. Updated October 9, 2026.

sources.title: Gemini API release notes — February 19, 2026
sources.evidence: The February 19, 2026 entry explicitly launches gemini-3.1-pro-preview-customtools alongside Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro model card
sources.evidence: The model card linked by the shared endpoint page identifies Gemini 3.1 Pro as a Google Gemini 3 reasoning model, distributes it through hosted products/APIs, and explicitly refers architecture to the Gemini 3 Pro card. No numerical parameter counts.

sources.title: Gemini 3 Pro model card — May 2026 update
sources.evidence: The architecture source explicitly referenced by the 3.1 Pro card describes a sparse mixture-of-experts Transformer. It explains per-token expert activation but provides no total or active count.

sources.title: Gemini API Additional Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Terms govern Gemini API access and prohibit extraction or replication of underlying model weights. They support the descriptive proprietary classification, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: Gemini Interactions API — model options
sources.evidence: Names the exact gemini-3.1-pro-preview-customtools model as Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview optimized for custom tool usage.

sources.title: Gemini CLI configuration — model definitions
sources.evidence: The exact customtools identifier has pro tier, gemini-3 family, thinking true and multimodalToolUse true; model-resolution rules explicitly select it for custom-tool use.

sources.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash model card — May 2026
sources.evidence: Later comparison table contains an explicitly labeled Gemini 3.1 Pro column, but reports benchmark results rather than total or active parameter counts.

sources.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash model card — September 2026
sources.evidence: Later card checked for model-size disclosures; its comparisons do not provide total or active parameter counts for Gemini 3.1 Pro or customtools.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon model card — October 2026
sources.evidence: Later card includes safety comparisons with Gemini 3.1 Pro; no numerical total or active parameter count for that model or customtools is disclosed.

sources.title: SFT Drives Gemini’s Safety Properties — June 13, 2026
sources.publisher: Josh Engels, Arthur Conmy, Bilal Chughtai and Neel Nanda — Google DeepMind Language Model Interpretability team
sources.evidence: First-party researcher update compares pretrained/SFT and production Gemini 3.1 Pro; it does not state customtools architecture changes or numerical model size. Inspected as training/interpretability evidence, not a source of transferred counts.

sources.title: Models.dev exact customtools record
sources.evidence: Original catalog lead inspected. Its display label and gemini-pro normalization are retained; factual specifications were checked against primary documentation.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro — Google Cloud model documentation
sources.evidence: Google Cloud lists the standard preview on February 19, 2026 and its customtools endpoint on February 23. The Gemini API changelog records both endpoints on February 19; the later Cloud date does not establish the earliest customtools release. Confirms standard-model context and capabilities.

name.note: Human-readable label for the explicitly documented customtools identifier.

developer.note: Google publishes this Gemini endpoint and its model card.

family.note: Catalog normalization for Gemini Pro; official CLI places this exact variant in the pro tier of Gemini 3.

release_date.note: The Gemini API changelog launches the exact endpoint on February 19. Google Cloud lists February 23 for its own endpoint; the earlier API release is retained.

open_weights.note: Hosted API/product distribution under restrictive terms; no downloadable weights are offered for this variant.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the model/API terms; documentation and client-code licenses are separate.

parameters_b.note: No numerical total disclosed in the inspected model cards, later comparisons, or first-party training research; targeted exact-name searches found no primary count.

active_parameters_b.note: Sparse expert activation is described, but no numerical active count is reported. Do not infer it from total size, benchmark scores, or unrelated research models.

architecture.note: Explicit chain: customtools is a version on the shared 3.1 Pro endpoint page, which links the 3.1 Pro card; that card delegates architecture to Gemini 3 Pro, documented as sparse MoE Transformer. No customtools-specific structural alteration is asserted.

context_window.note: Shared documented input-token limit applies to both listed preview versions; output limit is separately 65,536.

modalities.note: Shared supported data types for the listed endpoint versions.

reasoning.note: Official CLI explicitly enables thinking for the exact customtools identifier.

tool_call.note: Exact variant is expressly optimized for custom tool selection and supports multimodal tool use.

description.value: Variant of Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview tuned to prefer custom tools in workflows that also use bash.
description.note: Replaces generic promotional wording with the documented distinguishing behavior.

patch.notes: Customtools is the separately named API variant for custom-tool prioritization. Sparse MoE Transformer architecture follows the explicitly linked shared model-card chain; total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed in the inspected primary evidence.

summary: Confirmed the exact customtools launch on February 19, 2026 and documented capabilities. Added proprietary classification and sparse MoE architecture through an explicit endpoint-to-model-card chain; made description variant-specific. Total and active counts remain undisclosed after checking later comparison cards and first-party training/interpretability research. Documentation was verified; current endpoint operation was not tested.
